name: Shackleton Crater Rim
geological_context: Impact crater rim bordering a Permanently Shadowed Region (PSR). Direct access to ultra-cold volatile/water-ice traps within 2.5 km traverse distance. Basaltic anorthosite regolith.
hazards: Steep 30-degree slopes into crater interior requiring tethered rover systems
Low sun elevation angles causing severe elongated shadows
scientific_significance: Key Artemis III/IV exploration candidate; cold traps preserve primordial solar system volatile delivery records.

name: Malapert Mountain (Peak of Eternal Light)
geological_context: Elevated massif providing near-continuous solar illumination and uninterrupted line-of-sight communication with Earth. 15 km from Faustini crater ice deposits.
hazards: Transit distance to permanently shadowed water ice (>12 km)
Micrometeorite exposure due to high topographic prominence
scientific_significance: Optimal telecommunications relay & early power station node for lunar polar network.

name: Marius Hills Lava Tube Skylight
geological_context: Subsurface collapsed volcanic lava conduit (skylight). Vast subterranean void (~100m wide, 40m ceiling) formed by ancient mare basalt volcanic flows.
hazards: Vertical shaft ingress/egress requiring hoists or elevator systems
Complete darkness within subsurface tube requiring artificial illumination and beamed power
scientific_significance: Perfect natural radiation, micrometeorite, and thermal shelter for long-duration permanent settlement.

name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton-de Gerlache)
geological_context: Narrow morphological ridge connecting two major polar impact structures. Excellent multi-directional traverse pathways for pressurized rovers.
hazards: Narrow landing corridor bounded by steep declivities
Occasional eclipse events (lunar dusk) requiring 54-72 hours of battery reserve
Severe abrasive regolith wear on rover seals
scientific_significance: Artemis III designated science area; provides dual access to both Shackleton and de Gerlache micro-environments.

name: Faustini Crater Rim
geological_context: Complex degraded impact crater harboring extensive radar-reflective volatile deposits verified by LRO Mini-RF and LAMP instruments.
hazards: Moderate direct-to-Earth communication occultation during lunar librations
Cryogenic frost migration hazards on solar panel hinges
scientific_significance: High concentration of organic volatiles and nitrogen-bearing compounds trapped alongside water ice.
